name: Gender, Youth and Inclusion
summary: How agri-energy programmes address the specific needs and opportunities for women, youth, and marginalised groups in Uganda's agri-energy sector.
description: Women, youth, and marginalised communities — including refugees and persons with disabilities — participate differently in agri-energy value chains and often have unequal access to technologies, financing, and information. This thematic area documents how agri-energy projects and programmes are addressing inclusion, what approaches have worked, and where gaps remain. Topics covered include gender-responsive design in technology deployment, women's enterprise models in agri-processing and cold chain, youth engagement in solar installation and maintenance businesses, and energy access for vulnerable populations including refugees and host communities.
whyItMatters: Agri-energy investments that ignore gender and social inclusion dynamics frequently miss the most energy-burdened populations — often women and youth — and lose opportunities for more equitable and sustainable impact. Evidence shows that gender-responsive agri-energy programming can dramatically improve project sustainability and amplify household-level benefits.
